senses.sense_definition: A hardened area of skin caused by repeated friction or pressure.

examples.text: The guitarist developed a thick <w>callus</w> on each fingertip from years of daily practice.
Wearing tight shoes for long periods often causes a painful <w>callus</w> to form on the heel.

senses.sense_definition: The new bony tissue that forms around a fracture during the healing process.

examples.text: The X-ray showed that a healthy <w>callus</w> had formed around the broken bone.
Doctors monitor the development of the <w>callus</w> to ensure the bone is knitting together correctly.

senses.sense_definition: A mass of undifferentiated cells that forms over a plant cutting before roots develop.

examples.text: The gardener waited for a <w>callus</w> to appear on the stem before planting the cutting in soil.
Proper humidity helps the plant cutting produce a <w>callus</w> instead of rotting.

senses.sense_definition: A fleshy outgrowth found on the labellum of an orchid flower.

examples.text: The unique shape of the <w>callus</w> helps identify this specific species of orchid.
Pollinators are often attracted to the bright colors of the orchid's <w>callus</w>.

senses.sense_definition: A hardened extension at the base of a grass floret.

examples.text: Botanists examine the <w>callus</w> of the floret to distinguish between different types of wild grasses.
The sharp <w>callus</w> helps the seed attach itself to the fur of passing animals.

senses.sense_definition: A shiny area on the forehead of certain types of flies.

examples.text: The size and color of the <w>callus</w> are key features for identifying horse flies.
Under the microscope, the <w>callus</w> on the fly's head appears smooth and reflective.

senses.sense_definition: To develop hardened skin due to repeated friction or pressure.

examples.text: If you play the violin every day, your fingertips will eventually <w>callus</w>.
The manual laborer's hands began to <w>callus</w> after weeks of heavy lifting.
